transcript.text: I made one cardinal mistake of starting
a business with a person who has the
same experience, the same time
commitment, and the same money. Yeah,
how would we think about separating the
roles between the two of us now?
>> The problem is if neither of you can
agree on what the role needs to be in
the business. And so Leila and I both
started with a sales background. It just
was like one of us had to make the call,
one of us is going to be in charge of
marketing sales, the other one is going
to be in charge of delivery and and
team. And so Leila just took the
delivery and team and I took the
marketing and sales and that's how we
split it. So I don't think it's that if
you have the same skill set coming in,
you can't do it. It's just that you need
to quickly differentiate and specialize
your role so that you can put all your
focus towards the thing that matters
most or that is the constraint for the
business. And then as long as you both
keep your ends of the of the deal and
you both work your asses off for it then
it could be a great partnership. If one
of you doesn't work as hard then it
becomes an issue.
